question: By selling an article at (8)/(13) of its actual selling price, Ramesh incurs a loss of 20%. If he sells it at 85% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Actual Selling Price (SP) = 130 units.

First SP = 8/13 × 130 = 80 units.

As the loss is 20%, Cost Price (CP) = 80 ÷ 0.80 = 100 units.

New SP = 85% of Actual SP = 0.85 × 130 = 110.5 units.

Profit % = New SP − CP = 110.5 − 100 = 10.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 10.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price 1 (SP₁) = 8/13 × Actual SP

Loss % at SP₁ = 20%

Selling Price 2 (SP₂) = 85% of Actual SP

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Loss%)

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100
